text:
sam: Hey team — customer reports invoice shows ~18k embedding units for April but dashboard usage shows ~6k. They only call /embeddings in batches of 8 and do pairwise reranking separately. Can we check why invoice > UI by ~3x?

lina: Which account? any sample request payloads or timestamps?

sam: acct_7F4Z, sample payload attached from customer (they redacted PII):
```json
{
  "model": "embed-large-v2",
  "input": ["doc1", "doc2", "doc3", "doc4", "doc5", "doc6", "doc7", "doc8"],
  "batch_size": 8
}
```

sam: They also run a separate rerank call that sends pairwise inputs: 1 query + 100 candidates -> they said API is /rerank with pairwise=true, which we account as pairwise but invoice looks like it's charging per-candidate twice? not sure.

lina: Noted. Can you paste the exact timestamps of the spike on the invoice and the dashboard range (to compare line items)?

sam: Invoice line items show heavy usage on 2026-04-14 02:00-06:00 UTC. Dashboard for acct_7F4Z shows small steady usage, peak aligned to 02:15 but only ~2k units at that hour.

jordan: Quick checklist: 1) Are retries creating duplicate counts? 2) Is pairwise rerank being sent as separate embedding calls under the hood? 3) Are inputs getting unintentionally duplicated by the client batching loop?

sam: Customer says they do exponential backoff but only on 5xx. They saw 429s earlier and client retries immediately (up to 2 retries). Could retries explain 3x gap?

lina: Retries could, but 3x seems high unless each request retried multiple times. We need the raw request_ids for that window. Can support provide request logs? @kai can you pull storage logs for acct_7F4Z 2026-04-14 01:30-06:30 UTC and grep for /embeddings and /rerank?

kai: Pulling now. Preliminary: I see a burst of many small embedding requests between 02:12-02:20 that were retries from the client — ~900 successful + ~1.8k retried attempts (so ~2.7k total). But that still doesn't reach 18k. Also found repeated rerank pairwise jobs that used pairwise=true but client-side expanded pairs before calling our API, so count shows up as N*100 instead of a single pairwise job.

sam: Wait — they said they send pairwise to /rerank. If they expanded pairs client-side, that would massively increase charge units. Can we find the request bodies?

kai: I pulled a few request samples: one rerank call shows body:
```json
{ "endpoint": "/rerank", "pairwise": false, "inputs": [ ["q1","cand1"], ["q1","cand2"], ... ] }
```
kai: So client set pairwise=false but passed pre-expanded pairs. Billing treats each input as a separate embedding/rerank call.

jordan: That explains delta. Invoices count per input vectors produced. If client pre-expanded pairs into 100 pair entries, that's 100x per query.

lina: Two action items: 1) Ask customer to confirm client behavior and share their code path for building rerank payloads. 2) Support asks billing for a line-item export for that invoice window to map request_ids -> billed units. @kai please attach CSV of request_id, endpoint, inputs_count, billed_units.

sam: I messaged customer asking for code snippet and their client version. They've sent a snippet showing they map candidates -> pairs before calling /rerank. So it's confirmed. They misunderstood 'pairwise' flag docs.

jordan: We should update docs to clarify server-side pairwise vs client expansion. Also add a small warning in SDKs for common pattern.

lina: For now, customer wants a goodwill review. Billing, can we offer credit for accidental duplicates if it's clearly client expansion and not malicious? @kai?

kai: I'll prepare the export. Policy: credits are exceptional; we need to verify pattern and how long it happened. If it's a one-off config mistake and they've been cooperative, billing can offer partial credit. I'll file ticket BILL-2026-433 and attach logs.

sam: Customer appreciates rapid triage. They asked for short repro steps to avoid future hits. Can we provide a checklist?

jordan: Repro checklist to send: 1) show client payload for rerank; 2) ensure pairwise=true if sending query+candidate pairs in single abstract call (server expands pairs), or if you pre-expand, set pairwise=false and expect per-pair billing; 3) prefer server-side pairwise with small batch sizes to reduce expansion; 4) include request_id header for traceability; 5) upgrade SDK to v2.3.1 which logs retries and will avoid immediate retry on 429 by default.

lina: I'll send that checklist + sample code diff and escalate billing ticket. Sam, can you confirm customer will accept partial credit review?

sam: Yes, they agreed to the review and will share code. Will follow up in this thread with their snippet and timeline. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Ticket BILL-2026-433 created. Assignee: kai. Priority: P2.

sam: thanks all — will paste customer code when I get it.

[end of thread]
